text: Nora is my dad's mum. Who is Nora? Build a full sentence. Start with She.
She is my grandmother.
Alex is my mum's dad. Who is Alex? Build a full sentence. Start with He.
He is my grandfather.
Nora and Max are my dad's mum and dad. Who are Nora and Max? Build a full sentence. Start with They.
They are my grandparents.
Ruth is my mum's mum. Who is Ruth? Say a full sentence.
She is my grandmother.
Owen is my dad's dad. Who is Owen? Say a full sentence.
He is my grandfather.
Ruth and Owen are my mum's mum and dad. Who are Ruth and Owen? Say a full sentence.
They are my grandparents.
Grace is your mum's mum. Who is Grace?
She is my grandmother.
Now talk about your mum's mum and dad together.
They are my grandparents.
Ben is your dad's dad. Fix one word.
He is my grandfather.
There are dolls on a shelf. A ball is next to a toy boat. What is this story about? Build a full sentence. Start with It.
It is about toys.
A small home has a green door. It has a kitchen and two rooms. What is this story about? Build a full sentence. Start with It.
It is about a house.
Two sisters help their dad. Their mum helps them too. What is this story about? Build a full sentence. Start with It.
It is about a family.
A teddy bear is on the bed. A toy train is on the floor. What is this story about? Say a full sentence.
It is about toys.
This home has a yellow door. A bedroom is next to the kitchen. What is this story about? Say a full sentence.
It is about a house.
A mum reads with her son. His sister sits with their dad. What is this story about? Say a full sentence.
It is about a family.
A toy car and a doll are in a box. What is the story about?
It is about toys.
Now there are two stories about toys. Change the sentence.
They are about toys.
Mum and Dad play with their son. Fix one word.
It is about a family.
Look at the picture. Tell me what you see. Build a full sentence. Start with There.
There is one book.
Look at the picture. Tell me what you see. Build a full sentence. Start with There.
There are four hats.
Look at the picture. Tell me what you see. Build a full sentence. Start with There.
There are two toys.
Look at the picture. Tell me what you see. Say a full sentence.
There is one tree.
Look at the picture. Tell me what you see. Say a full sentence.
There are five dogs.
Look at the picture. Tell me what you see. Say a full sentence.
There are three cats.
Look at the picture and build a sentence.
There are three cats.
There are three cats, and two go away. What is left?
There is one cat.
Look at the two dogs and fix one word.
There are two dogs.
The number is twelve. Is it odd or even? Build a full sentence. Start with Twelve.
Twelve is an even number.
The number is eleven. Is it odd or even? Build a full sentence. Start with Eleven.
Eleven is an odd number.
The number is fourteen. Is it odd or even? Build a full sentence. Start with Fourteen.
Fourteen is an even number.
The number is thirteen. Is it odd or even? Say a full sentence.
Thirteen is an odd number.
The number is sixteen. Is it odd or even? Say a full sentence.
Sixteen is an even number.
The number is fifteen. Is it odd or even? Say a full sentence.
Fifteen is an odd number.
Is eighteen odd or even? Build a sentence.
Eighteen is an even number.
Add one to eighteen. Is the new number odd or even?
Nineteen is an odd number.
Is twenty odd or even? Fix one word.
Twenty is an even number.
There are six books. The box has room for four books. Why will they not all fit? Build a full sentence. Start with There.
There are too many books.
There are five toys. The box has room for two toys. Why will they not all fit? Build a full sentence. Start with There.
There are too many toys.
There are seven hats. The box has room for five hats. Why will they not all fit? Build a full sentence. Start with There.
There are too many hats.
There are eight books. The box has room for five books. Why will they not all fit? Say a full sentence.
There are too many books.
There are six toys. The box has room for three toys. Why will they not all fit? Say a full sentence.
There are too many toys.
There are four hats. The box has room for two hats. Why will they not all fit? Say a full sentence.
There are too many hats.
The box holds six books, but you have eight. Describe the problem.
There are too many books.
There are eight books, and you take two out. How many remain?
There are six books.
There is room for four toys, but you have seven. Fix one word.
There are too many toys.
Pretend you are Pat. Amy is your dad's sister. Who is Amy in your pretend family? Build a full sentence. Start with Amy.
Amy is my aunt.
Pretend you are Pat. Dan is your mum's brother. Who is Dan in your pretend family? Build a full sentence. Start with Dan.
Dan is my uncle.
Pretend you are Pat. Joe is your aunt's son. Who is Joe in your pretend family? Build a full sentence. Start with Joe.
Joe is my cousin.
Pretend you are Pat. Eva is your mum's sister. Who is Eva in your pretend family? Say a full sentence.
Eva is my aunt.
Pretend you are Pat. Rob is your dad's brother. Who is Rob in your pretend family? Say a full sentence.
Rob is my uncle.
Pretend you are Pat. May is your uncle's daughter. Who is May in your pretend family? Say a full sentence.
May is my cousin.
Sue is your mum's sister. Who is Sue?
She is my aunt.
Now talk about your mum's brother. Change the sentence.
He is my uncle.
Max is your aunt's son. Fix one word.
He is my cousin.
I am happy. Make the sentence short. Build a full sentence.
I'm happy.
He is my cousin. Make the sentence short. Build a full sentence.
He's my cousin.
I am ten years old. Make the sentence short. Build a full sentence.
I'm ten years old.
He is happy. Make the sentence short. Say a full sentence.
He's happy.
I am your friend. Make the sentence short. Say a full sentence.
I'm your friend.
He is eight years old. Make the sentence short. Say a full sentence.
He's eight years old.
He is my friend. Make it short.
He's my friend.
I'm happy. Make it long.
I am happy.
You are happy. Fix one word.
I'm happy.
The word is cold. Name its opposite. Build a full sentence.
Hot is the opposite of cold.
The word is big. Name its opposite. Build a full sentence.
Small is the opposite of big.
The word is young. Name its opposite. Build a full sentence.
Old is the opposite of young.
The word is hot. Name its opposite. Say a full sentence.
Cold is the opposite of hot.
The word is small. Name its opposite. Say a full sentence.
Big is the opposite of small.
The word is old. Name its opposite. Say a full sentence.
Young is the opposite of old.
What is the opposite of cold? Keep cold at the end.
Hot is the opposite of cold.
Change the sentence to start with The.
The opposite of old is young.
Keep Small and fix the last word.
Small is the opposite of big.
Your task is to carry books to school. Which tool can help? Build a full sentence. Start with I.
I use a backpack to carry books.
Your task is to write a story on paper. Which tool can help? Build a full sentence. Start with I.
I use a notebook to write a story.
Your task is to draw a straight line. Which tool can help? Build a full sentence. Start with I.
I use a ruler to draw a line.
Your task is to erase a pencil line. What do you use, and why? Say a full sentence.
I use an eraser to erase the line.
Your task is to carry pencils and books. What do you use, and why? Say a full sentence.
I use a backpack to carry pencils and books.
Your task is to find a small book for writing a list. What do you use, and why? Say a full sentence.
I use a notebook to write a list.
You want to erase a pencil mark. Which tool can help?
I use an eraser.
Now you want to draw a straight line. Change the sentence.
I use a ruler.
You want to carry books to school. Fix one word.
I use a backpack.
Mia has four erasers. Leo has five erasers. How many erasers do they have together? Build a full sentence. Start with They.
They have nine erasers.
Mia has six notebooks. Leo has two notebooks. How many notebooks do they have together? Build a full sentence. Start with They.
They have eight notebooks.
Mia has five rulers. Leo has six rulers. How many rulers do they have together? Build a full sentence. Start with They.
They have eleven rulers.
Mia has seven pencils. Leo has three pencils. How many pencils do they have together? Say a full sentence.
They have ten pencils.
Mia has four pens. Leo has eight pens. How many pens do they have together? Say a full sentence.
They have twelve pens.
Mia has five erasers. Leo has two erasers. How many erasers do they have together? Say a full sentence.
They have seven erasers.
Amy has three pencils and Ben has four. How many altogether?
They have seven pencils.
Now you are Amy. How many pencils do you have?
I have three pencils.
Amy has two rulers and Ben has three. Fix one word.
They have five rulers.
Tom and Ann say, four backpacks, five backpacks, six backpacks. What are they doing now? Build a full sentence. Start with They.
They are counting backpacks.
Tom and Ann say, four notebooks, five notebooks, six notebooks. What are they doing now? Build a full sentence. Start with They.
They are counting notebooks.
Tom and Ann say, four pens, five pens, six pens. What are they doing now? Build a full sentence. Start with They.
They are counting pens.
Tom and Ann say, four rulers, five rulers, six rulers. What are they doing now? Say a full sentence.
They are counting rulers.
Tom and Ann say, four pencils, five pencils, six pencils. What are they doing now? Say a full sentence.
They are counting pencils.
Tom and Ann say, four erasers, five erasers, six erasers. What are they doing now? Say a full sentence.
They are counting erasers.
Dan and Sue say one book, two books, three books. What are they doing?
They are counting books.
Now Sue is alone with hats. Change the sentence.
She is counting hats.
Kim and Pat count toys together. Fix one word.
They are counting toys.
Pretend you are Jo. Jo and Lee are both eleven years old. Tell Lee that your ages are the same. Build a full sentence. Start with I.
I am eleven years old too.
Pretend you are Jo. Jo and Lee are both twelve years old. Tell Lee that your ages are the same. Build a full sentence. Start with I.
I am twelve years old too.
Pretend you are Jo. Jo and Lee are both thirteen years old. Tell Lee that your ages are the same. Build a full sentence. Start with I.
I am thirteen years old too.
Pretend you are Jo. Jo and Lee are both fourteen years old. Tell Lee that your ages are the same. Say a full sentence.
I am fourteen years old too.
Pretend you are Jo. Jo and Lee are both fifteen years old. Tell Lee that your ages are the same. Say a full sentence.
I am fifteen years old too.
Pretend you are Jo. Jo and Lee are both sixteen years old. Tell Lee that your ages are the same. Say a full sentence.
I am sixteen years old too.
You and Pat are both nine. Tell Pat your age.
I am nine years old too.
You are nine, but Pat is ten. Tell Pat your age.
I am nine years old.
You and Kim are both eight. Fix one word.
I am eight years old too.
This pretend plan is for fall. The plan is to plant flowers. Tell me the plan. Build a full sentence. Start with I.
I plant flowers in fall.
This pretend plan is for winter. The plan is to ride a bike. Tell me the plan. Build a full sentence. Start with I.
I ride a bike in winter.
This pretend plan is for spring. The plan is to eat ice cream. Tell me the plan. Build a full sentence. Start with I.
I eat ice cream in spring.
This pretend plan is for summer. The plan is to fly a kite. What do you do in this plan? Say a full sentence.
I fly a kite in summer.
This pretend plan is for fall. The plan is to drink hot chocolate. What do you do in this plan? Say a full sentence.
I drink hot chocolate in fall.
This pretend plan is for winter. The plan is to go to the beach. What do you do in this plan? Say a full sentence.
I go to the beach in winter.
Look at your winter plan and build a sentence starting with I.
I fly a kite in winter.
Tell the same plan, but start with In.
In summer I plant flowers.
Look at your spring plan and fix one word.
I ride a bike in spring.
Three things: rulers, erasers, and notebooks. Which written sentence uses commas to separate the list?
I see rulers, erasers, and notebooks.
Three things: cats, birds, and trees. Which written sentence uses commas to separate the list?
I see cats, birds, and trees.
Three things: toys, books, and pencils. Which written sentence uses commas to separate the list?
I see toys, books, and pencils.
The list is blue, red, and yellow. Name all three colors in one sentence. Do not say the word comma. Say a full sentence.
The colors are blue, red, and yellow.
The list is pens, rulers, and erasers. Name all three things in one sentence. Do not say the word comma. Say a full sentence.
I see pens, rulers, and erasers.
The list is summer, fall, and winter. Tell me the three seasons in this pretend plan. Do not say the word comma. Say a full sentence.
I like summer, fall, and winter.
Put pens first and books last. Build a list sentence.
I see pens and books.
Add rulers between pens and books. Use commas in your list.
I see pens, rulers, and books.
Look at the three things and fix the comma.
I see cats, dogs, and birds.
